NOT FOR RELEASE, PUBLICATION OR DISTRIBUTION, IN WHOLE OR IN PART, IN OR INTO OR TO ANY PERSON LOCATED OR RESIDENT IN THE UNITED STATES, ITS TERRITORIES AND POSSESSIONS (INCLUDING PUERTO RICO, THE U.S. VIRGIN ISLANDS, GUAM, AMERICAN SAMOA, WAKE ISLAND AND THE NORTHERN MARIANA ISLANDS), ANY STATE OF THE UNITED STATES OR THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA (THE "UNITED STATES") OR TO ANY U.S. PERSON (AS DEFINED BELOW) OR IN OR INTO ANY OTHER JURISDICTION WHERE IT IS UNLAWFUL TO DISTRIBUTE THIS ANNOUNCEMENT.

This announcement contains inside information as defined in Article 7 of the Market Abuse Regulation (EU) 596/2014 as it forms part of United Kingdom domestic law by virtue of the European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018, as amended ("MAR"). Upon the publication of this announcement via Regulatory News Service, this inside information will be considered to be in the public domain. This announcement has been authorised for release by Mr. Ramez MHD Ruslan Alkhayyat, Vice Chairman of Estithmar Holding Q.P.S.C.
2 September 2026
ESTITHMAR HOLDING Q.P.S.C. ANNOUNCES EXCHANGE OFFER AND CONSENT SOLICITATION
Estithmar Holding Q.P.S.C.
(established in Qatar on 11 May 2008 as a Qatari limited liability company and converted to a Qatari public shareholding company on 11 May 2017)
("Estithmar")
to the holders of the following trust certificates (the "Certificateholders"):
Description of Trust Certificates
QAR 900,000,000 Trust Certificates due September 2027[1]
ISIN
Aggregate Face Amount Outstanding

Capitalised terms used but not otherwise defined in this announcement shall have the meanings given to them in the Exchange Offer and Consent Solicitation Memorandum dated 2 September 2026 (the "Offer Memorandum").
Estithmar, today, announces invitations to:

(i) Eligible Certificateholders to offer their Existing Certificates for exchange for new Qatari Riyal denominated Certificates due 2029  (the "New Certificates") to be issued by Estithmar Sukuk Limited LLC (the "Trustee") under its QAR 3,400,000,000 Trust Certificate Issuance Programme, as updated, subject to the satisfaction or waiver of the conditions described in the Offer Memorandum (the "Exchange Offer"); and

(ii) all Certificateholders to consent to certain modifications to the Pricing Supplements relating to the Existing Certificates by approving an Extraordinary Resolution initially by way of Electronic Consent and, if the Extraordinary Resolution is not passed by way of Electronic Consent by the Electronic Consent Deadline, at the Meeting (the "Consent Solicitation" and, together with the Exchange Offer, the "Invitation").

For the avoidance of doubt, the proposed modifications do not themselves constitute a notice of redemption of the Existing Certificates or an obligation on Estithmar to exercise any Optional Dissolution Right.

The Electronic Consent process and the Meeting process will run in parallel. Eligible Certificateholders may submit an Exchange Instruction and Certificateholders may submit a Voting Instruction. Exchange Instructions and Voting Instructions will be used for the purposes of determining whether the Extraordinary Resolution has been passed by way of Electronic Consent and, if the Extraordinary Resolution is not passed by way of Electronic Consent by the Electronic Consent Deadline and the Meeting proceeds, will automatically be treated as instructions for the purposes of the Meeting without any further action being required by the relevant Certificateholder.

Eligible Certificateholders who submit Exchange Instructions will be deemed to give Electronic Consent in favour of the Extraordinary Resolution and, if the Meeting proceeds, to vote in favour of the Extraordinary Resolution at the Meeting. Certificateholders that do not wish to participate in the Exchange Offer may submit Voting Instructions in favour of or against the Extraordinary Resolution.

The Exchange Offer is being made at an exchange ratio of QAR 1,000,000 in face amount of Existing Certificates for QAR 1,000,000 in face amount of New Certificates, together with payment of the Accrued Periodic Distribution Amount in respect of Existing Certificates validly offered and accepted for exchange. Settlement of the Exchange Offer is expected to occur on the Early Settlement Date or the Settlement Date, as applicable, subject in each case to the terms and conditions of the Offer Memorandum.

Estithmar shall not be obliged to accept any Existing Certificates offered for exchange and, subject to the terms of the Offer Memorandum, acceptance by Estithmar of any Existing Certificates validly offered for exchange is in Estithmar's sole discretion and is subject to, among other things, the Extraordinary Resolution being passed and becoming effective pursuant to the Proposal (as defined below), whether by way of Electronic Consent or, if applicable, at the Meeting (or any adjourned Meeting).
Background and Rationale
Overview of Estithmar

Estithmar Holding Q.P.S.C. is a leading conglomerate headquartered in Qatar and a holding company that manages a portfolio of subsidiary companies operating across a diverse range of sectors, conducting its business through its subsidiaries (together with Estithmar, the "Group"). The Existing Certificates were issued in four tranches under the Programme: Tranche 1 (in the face amount of QAR 500,000,000) issued on 2 September 2024, Tranche 2 (in the face amount of QAR 145,000,000) issued on 16 December 2024, Tranche 3 (in the face amount of QAR 150,000,000) issued on 15 October 2025, and Tranche 4 (in the face amount of QAR 105,000,000) issued on 16 March 2026, each fungible and forming part of a single series under ISIN XS2884005047, with a scheduled dissolution date of 2 September 2027, and an aggregate outstanding face amount of QAR 900,000,000.

The New Certificates are expected to be issued, subject to completion of the Exchange Offer and the applicable conditions, under the Programme, as updated, in an aggregate face amount of up to QAR 1,000,000,000, will bear a profit rate of 9.00 per cent. per annum, and will have a tenure of 3 years.
Exchange Offer

Pursuant to the Exchange Offer, Eligible Certificateholders are invited to exchange their Existing Certificates for New Certificates. The New Certificates will be issued under the Programme, as updated, on the same Mudaraba-Murabaha structure and governed by English law, as with the Existing Certificates. However, the New Certificates will have a later maturity date, a higher profit rate and will otherwise be issued on terms that differ from those applicable to the Existing Certificates in certain respects. The Exchange Offer is intended to manage the maturity profile of the Group's financing arrangements, raise incremental funding for the Group's ongoing business activities, widen the Group's investor base and support the Group's broader capital management objectives.
Consent Solicitation and Proposal

In connection with the Exchange Offer, Estithmar is also seeking the approval of Certificateholders by way of an Extraordinary Resolution pursuant to the Master Trust Deed for the activation of the Optional Dissolution Right in respect of the Existing Certificates (the "Proposal"), initially by way of Electronic Consent and, if the Extraordinary Resolution is not passed by way of Electronic Consent by the Electronic Consent Deadline, at the Meeting, as more fully described in the Offer Memorandum. The Proposal contemplates the designation of the Optional Dissolution Right as "Applicable" in respect of the Existing Certificates.

Under the Conditions, whether the Optional Dissolution Right applies to a particular series of Certificates is determined by the applicable Pricing Supplement. Item 17 (Optional Dissolution Right) of each of the Pricing Supplements currently specifies that the Optional Dissolution Right is "Not Applicable" to the Existing Certificates.

To give effect to the Proposal, Item 17 (Optional Dissolution Right) of each of the Pricing Supplements would, if the Extraordinary Resolution is passed and becomes effective, be amended by deleting the words "Not Applicable" and replacing them with the word "Applicable" and to make certain consequential amendments to the provisions relating to the exercise of the Optional Dissolution Right, in each case as set out in the applicable Amended and Restated Pricing Supplement.

If the Extraordinary Resolution is passed and becomes effective, whether by way of Electronic Consent or, if applicable, at the Meeting (or any adjourned Meeting), Estithmar would have the ability (but not the obligation) to exercise the Optional Dissolution Right at the Dissolution Distribution Amount in accordance with the Conditions and the Amended and Restated Pricing Supplements in respect of Existing Certificates that remain outstanding following completion of the Exchange Offer. The Proposal would provide Estithmar with the ability, in its discretion and should it choose to do so, to redeem a residual amount of the Existing Certificates in full and at par, rather than leave a reduced size of Existing Certificates outstanding until their scheduled dissolution date.
The background to the Exchange Offer, Consent Solicitation and Proposal is more fully described in the Offer Memorandum, see further "Background and Rationale" therein.
Key Terms and Conditions of the Invitation
The Invitation commences on the date of this announcement.

The deadline for receipt by the Exchange and Tabulation Agent of Exchange Instructions and Voting Instructions from Certificateholders wishing to participate in the Electronic Consent process is 4:00 p.m. (London time) on 14 September 2026, being the Electronic Consent Deadline. If the Extraordinary Resolution is not passed by way of Electronic Consent by the Electronic Consent Deadline, Exchange Instructions and Voting Instructions may continue to be submitted until 4:00 p.m. (London time) on 21 September 2026, being the Final Deadline.

The Notice of Electronic Consent and Meeting convening the Meeting and circulating the Extraordinary Resolution by way of Electronic Consent has been given to Certificateholders (in accordance with the Conditions) on the date of this announcement.
Voting

To be approved by way of Electronic Consent, the Extraordinary Resolution requires consents in favour from Certificateholders representing not less than 75 per cent. in aggregate face amount of the Existing Certificates then outstanding. Delivery of an Exchange Instruction or Voting Instruction in respect of the Extraordinary Resolution for Electronic Consent is made upon valid submission of such instruction before the Electronic Consent Deadline. If the Extraordinary Resolution is passed by way of Electronic Consent, it will be binding on all Certificateholders whether or not they participated in the Electronic Consent process.

For the Extraordinary Resolution to be passed at a Meeting (or any adjourned Meeting), it will need to be passed at a Meeting of the Certificateholders duly convened, quorate and held by a majority in favour of not less than three-quarters of the persons voting thereat upon a show of hands or, if a poll is duly demanded, by a majority in favour consisting of not less than three-quarters of votes cast. The quorum requirement for the Meeting shall be one or more Eligible Persons present and holding or representing (i) at least 75 per cent. of the aggregate face amount of the Existing Certificates for the time being outstanding at the original Meeting; or (ii) at least 25 per cent. of the aggregate face amount of the Existing Certificates for the time being outstanding at any adjourned Meeting.

If the Extraordinary Resolution is passed by way of Electronic Consent: (i) Estithmar will announce whether and to what extent it will, subject to satisfaction or waiver of the Consent Condition and the other applicable terms and conditions of the Exchange Offer, accept for exchange Existing Certificates validly offered for exchange pursuant to Exchange Instructions received on or prior to the Electronic Consent Deadline and, if so accepted, the Early Settlement Date and (ii) the Meeting will be cancelled. If the Extraordinary Resolution is not passed by way of Electronic Consent by the Electronic Consent Deadline and the Meeting proceeds, Estithmar will announce the results of the Meeting (or any adjourned Meeting) and, if the Extraordinary Resolution is passed, announce, if then determined, the Settlement Date for the Exchange Offer as soon as reasonably practicable after the Meeting (or any adjourned Meeting).

If the Extraordinary Resolution is not passed by way of Electronic Consent, it will be considered at the Meeting to be held at the offices of Simmons & Simmons LLP at CityPoint, One Ropemaker Street, London EC2Y 9SS, United Kingdom at 12:00 p.m. (London time) on 24 September 2026. Any valid Exchange Instructions and Voting Instructions submitted before the Electronic Consent Deadline will remain valid and will automatically be used for the purposes of the Meeting without any further action being required by the relevant Certificateholder. In such circumstances, Certificateholders may continue to submit Exchange Instructions and Voting Instructions until the Final Deadline.

If the Extraordinary Resolution is passed by way of Electronic Consent or, if applicable, at the Meeting (or any adjourned Meeting), the Proposal will be binding on all Certificateholders, whether or not they gave Electronic Consent, attended or were otherwise represented at the Meeting and, if they attended or were represented at the Meeting, whether they voted in favour of or against the Extraordinary Resolution. Certificateholders who do not consent to the Proposal by way of Electronic Consent, or, if the Meeting proceeds, do not participate in the Meeting, will, if the Extraordinary Resolution is passed and becomes effective in accordance with its terms, nonetheless be bound by it.

Exchange Instructions must be submitted in respect of a minimum face amount of Existing Certificates of not less than QAR 1,000,000 and may be submitted in integral multiples of QAR 10,000 thereafter. Voting Instructions must be submitted in respect of a minimum face amount of Existing Certificates of QAR 10,000 and may be submitted in integral multiples of QAR 10,000 thereafter.
General

Set out below is an indicative timetable showing one possible outcome for the timing of the Exchange Offer, the Consent Solicitation and the Proposal, which will depend, among other things, on timely receipt (and non-revocation) of instructions, whether the Extraordinary Resolution is passed by way of Electronic Consent by the Electronic Consent Deadline or, if the Meeting proceeds, whether the Meeting is adjourned, the right of Estithmar to extend, re-open, amend and/or terminate the Exchange Offer, the Consent Solicitation and the Proposal (other than the terms of the Extraordinary Resolution) as described in the Offer Memorandum not being exercised and the passing of the Extraordinary Resolution. Accordingly, the actual timetable may differ significantly from the timetable below.

A complete description of the terms and conditions of the Invitation is set out in the Offer Memorandum. A copy of the Offer Memorandum is available to Certificateholders on the Invitation Website (https://deals.is.kroll.com/estithmar), subject to registration, and can be obtained from the Exchange and Tabulation Agent.

Before making a decision with respect to the Invitation, Certificateholders should carefully consider all of the information in the Offer Memorandum and, in particular, the risk factors described in the section entitled "Risk Factors and Other Considerations Relating to the Exchange Offer, the Consent Solicitation and the Proposal" therein.
